overall: The AG found the Charter Review Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by approving 2021 and 2022 minutes (and one May 2023 set) untimely, rejected its complaint-timeliness defense, found no violation for not posting minutes online, and ordered future compliance; the Committee had since approved and posted the minutes, so no further remedy.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Charter Review Committee failed to timely approve minutes of meetings held since February 2022; the Committee did not dispute the delay.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee’s approval of all of the 2021 and 2022 meetings, as well as the May 10, 2023, meeting, was untimely.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee violated the law by failing to post meeting minutes online.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to post minutes to a website, but rather to provide meeting minutes upon request within 10 days, if the minutes exist, whether approved or still in draft form.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
